title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 91
paragraphs: At this time, then, when the Lacedaemonians had recovered the oracles and saw that the Athenians were growing in power and were by no means willing to submit to them, and perceiving that the Athenian race, now that it was free, was becoming a match for their own—whereas when held down by tyrants it had been weak and ready to be ruled—perceiving, I say, all these things, they sent for Hippias son of Peisistratus to come from Sigeum on the Hellespont, to which the family of Peisistratus had fled for refuge. When Hippias had come at the summons, the Spartans also sent for envoys to come from their other allies, and spoke to them as follows: “Allies, we are conscious within ourselves that we have not acted rightly. For, incited by counterfeit oracles, we drove into exile men who were most closely united with us as guest-friends and who had undertaken to make Athens subject to us; then, after doing this, we handed over the state to a thankless populace, which, as soon as it had raised its head—having been freed by us—drove out us and our king with wanton outrage; and now, puffed up with pride, it is growing in power, so that the neighbors of these people have already learned this—first the Boeotians and Chalcidians—and perhaps others will learn it afterwards: that they made a mistake. Since, then, we erred in what has been described, we will now try, together with you, to take vengeance on them; for this is why we sent for Hippias, whom you see here, and for you to come from your cities, so that with common counsel and common force we might bring him to Athens and restore to him what we formerly took away.”
